subject: Auditing and Ethics
question_html: 'Audit risk', as used in the Standards on Auditing, means:

options.A: The risk that the auditor gives an inappropriate audit opinion when the financial statements are materially misstated
options.B: The risk that the client's business will fail within one year of the audit
options.C: The risk that the auditor's fee will not be recovered from the client
options.D: The risk that the client will change its auditor in the following year

answer_html:
A. The risk that the auditor gives an inappropriate audit opinion when the financial statements are materially misstated

Audit risk means the risk that the auditor gives an inappropriate audit opinion when the financial statements are materially misstated - for example, expressing an unmodified opinion when the financial statements are, in fact, materially misstated.

question_html: Risks of material misstatement at the overall financial statement level generally arise due to:

options.A: The auditor's own failure to charge an adequate audit fee
options.B: The entity's decision to use a particular brand of accounting software

question_html: 'Control risk', as described in SA 200, is:

options.A: The risk that the entity's internal control is entirely absent
options.B: The risk that the auditor fails to obtain a management representation letter
options.C: The risk that a misstatement that could occur in an assertion about a class of transaction, account balance or disclosure, and that could be material, will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis by the entity's internal control

answer_html:

Control risk is the risk that a misstatement that could occur in an assertion, and that could be material, will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis by the entity's internal control. There is an inverse relationship between control risk and the efficiency of internal control.

subject: Auditing and Ethics
question_html: Among audit risk, inherent risk, control risk and detection risk, which one can the auditor actually influence?

options.A: Detection risk alone; inherent risk and control risk belong to the entity and are influenced by the entity, not the auditor
options.B: Inherent risk alone, since it is entirely within the auditor's control
options.C: Control risk alone, since the auditor designs the entity's internal controls
options.D: All of inherent risk, control risk and detection risk equally

answer_html:
A. Detection risk alone; inherent risk and control risk belong to the entity and are influenced by the entity, not the auditor

Inherent risk and control risk are the entity's risks and exist independently of the audit; they are influenced by the client. The auditor can only influence detection risk, and must therefore reduce detection risk (through larger samples, more competent staff, etc.) to keep audit risk at an acceptably low level.

subject: Auditing and Ethics
question_html: Since risk of material misstatement is a function of inherent risk and control risk, audit risk can be expressed as:

options.A: Audit risk = Inherent risk + Control risk + Detection risk
options.B: Audit risk = Inherent risk x Control risk x Detection risk
options.C: Audit risk = Detection risk / Control risk
options.D: Audit risk = Inherent risk - Control risk + Detection risk

answer_html:
B. Audit risk = Inherent risk x Control risk x Detection risk

Since audit risk = Risk of material misstatement x Detection risk, and risk of material misstatement is itself a function of inherent risk and control risk, audit risk can also be expressed as: Audit risk = Inherent risk x Control risk x Detection risk.

question_html: In exercising judgment as to which identified risks are 'significant risks', the auditor shall consider at least which of the following?

answer_html:

subject: Auditing and Ethics
case_facts_html: Skyline Electronics Retail Ltd. operates a chain of stores selling mobile phones, laptops and other consumer electronics. Every item carries an RFID security tag, and physical stock counts are conducted quarterly at each store. During the audit, CA Devansh Rao notes that electronic goods are highly susceptible to theft and rapid obsolescence by their very nature. He also considers that, despite the RFID tags and quarterly counts, two or more store employees could potentially collude to bypass these controls. Finally, he plans to test a sample of transactions and perform physical observation, recognising that even these procedures may not detect every instance of stock loss.
question_html: CA Devansh Rao's observation that electronic goods are, by their very nature, highly susceptible to theft and rapid obsolescence - even before considering any controls the company has put in place - relates to which component of the risk of material misstatement?

options.A: Control risk, since it concerns the effectiveness of the RFID tags and quarterly counts
options.B: Detection risk, since it concerns the auditor's own sampling and observation procedures
options.C: Audit risk, since it concerns the auditor's overall opinion on the financial statements
options.D: Inherent risk, since it is the susceptibility of an assertion (such as existence or valuation of inventory) to material misstatement due to the very nature of the item, before consideration of any related controls

answer_html:
D. Inherent risk, since it is the susceptibility of an assertion (such as existence or valuation of inventory) to material misstatement due to the very nature of the item, before consideration of any related controls

Inherent risk is the susceptibility of an assertion to a misstatement that could be material, before consideration of any related controls. Assets such as easily saleable, high-turnover electronic goods are inherently more susceptible to theft and obsolescence, giving rise to higher inherent risk.

case_facts_html: Skyline Electronics Retail Ltd. operates a chain of stores selling mobile phones, laptops and other consumer electronics. question_html: CA Devansh Rao's recognition that his own sample-based testing and observation procedures may still fail to detect every instance of stock loss relates to which component of risk, and who can influence it?

options.A: Inherent risk, which the auditor can influence by redesigning the company's RFID tagging system
options.B: Detection risk - the risk that the auditor's own procedures fail to detect a material misstatement that exists; unlike inherent risk and control risk (which belong to the entity), detection risk is the one risk the auditor can influence, for example by increasing sample sizes or using more experienced staff
options.C: Control risk, which the auditor can influence by personally implementing new controls at the client's stores
options.D: Business risk, which is outside the scope of SA 200 entirely

answer_html:

Detection risk - the risk that the auditor's own procedures fail to detect a material misstatement that exists; unlike inherent risk and control risk (which belong to the entity), detection risk is the one risk the auditor can influence, for example by increasing sample sizes or using more experienced staff

Detection risk is the risk that the auditor's procedures will not detect an existing material misstatement. Inherent risk and control risk belong to the entity and are influenced by the entity; the auditor can only influence detection risk, which can be reduced by increasing the area of checking, testing larger samples, and involving more competent and experienced staff.

subject: Auditing and Ethics
case_facts_html: Meridian Consumer Foods Ltd. has a profit before tax of ₹40 crore for the year. While planning the audit, CA Ishita Bhalla determines overall materiality for the financial statements as a whole at ₹1.6 crore. During fieldwork, she identifies several individually immaterial misstatements: inventory overstated by ₹45 lakh, trade payables understated by ₹40 lakh, and a provision for warranty claims understated by ₹35 lakh. Individually, each of these is well below the overall materiality of ₹1.6 crore, but CA Bhalla is concerned that, taken together, such misstatements could approach or exceed it. She had, at the planning stage itself, set a lower threshold of ₹60 lakh to guide the nature, timing and extent of her audit procedures.
question_html: The ₹60 lakh threshold that CA Ishita Bhalla set at the planning stage, lower than the overall materiality of ₹1.6 crore, is best described as:

options.A: Overall materiality itself, merely expressed using a different figure
options.B: Audit risk, expressed in monetary rather than percentage terms
options.C: Performance materiality - an amount set by the auditor at less than overall materiality, to reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds materiality for the financial statements as a whole
options.D: Control risk, quantified for the purposes of this specific engagement

answer_html:
C. Performance materiality - an amount set by the auditor at less than overall materiality, to reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds materiality for the financial statements as a whole

Performance materiality is the amount set by the auditor at less than materiality for the financial statements as a whole, to reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds overall materiality - exactly the purpose served by CA Bhalla's ₹60 lakh threshold.

question_html: Why is CA Ishita Bhalla concerned about the individually immaterial misstatements identified in inventory, trade payables and the warranty provision, even though none of them individually exceeds ₹1.6 crore?

options.A: Because each individual misstatement, considered alone, already exceeds the overall materiality of ₹1.6 crore
options.B: Because SA 320 requires every misstatement, however small, to be separately reported to those charged with governance regardless of aggregation
options.C: Because the misstatements relate exclusively to related party transactions, which are always material irrespective of amount
options.D: Because it is likely that misstatements are material in the aggregate; several small misstatements in different account balances may individually be immaterial but could become material when aggregated, which is precisely the concern that performance materiality is designed to address

answer_html:
D. Because it is likely that misstatements are material in the aggregate; several small misstatements in different account balances may individually be immaterial but could become material when aggregated, which is precisely the concern that performance materiality is designed to address

Practically, it is difficult for auditors to design tests to identify individual material misstatements; it is likely that misstatements are material in the aggregate. Performance materiality, set lower than overall materiality, is specifically designed to reduce the probability that such aggregated uncorrected/undetected misstatements exceed overall materiality.

question_html: Suppose that, midway through the audit, one of Meridian Consumer Foods Ltd.'s manufacturing units is destroyed in a fire, causing actual results to differ substantially from the anticipated year-end results used to originally determine materiality. What should CA Ishita Bhalla do?

options.A: Revise the materiality for the financial statements as a whole (and, if a lower materiality is now appropriate, determine whether performance materiality also needs revision, and whether the nature, timing and extent of further audit procedures remain appropriate)
options.B: Continue to use the original materiality figure without any revision, since materiality is fixed permanently once determined at the planning stage
options.C: Abandon the audit engagement entirely, since a fire is an event outside the auditor's professional competence
options.D: Automatically issue a disclaimer of opinion, without considering revision of materiality at all

Materiality for the financial statements as a whole may need to be revised as a result of a change in circumstances during the audit, new information, or a change in the auditor's understanding. If actual results differ substantially from those anticipated, the auditor revises materiality, and, if a lower materiality is appropriate, considers whether performance materiality and the nature/timing/extent of further procedures also need revision.

question_html: CA Rehaan Mistry's consideration of the competitive environment in precision farming and the new agri-data privacy regulations relates to which aspect of understanding the entity and its environment, as per SA 315?

question_html: Regarding internal financial controls at Farida Home Textiles Ltd. (a listed company), which of the following correctly describes the respective responsibilities under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.C: Internal financial controls reporting requirements apply uniformly to every company, including One Person Companies and small companies, without any exemption

answer_html:
A.
